chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there [a ruling] regarding rice?' He said, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'Indeed, Medina was not a land of rice at that time, so the ruling would not be said regarding it; but it has been established regarding it. And how could it not be, since the majority of the land tax (kharaj) of Iraq is from it?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for rice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the zakat liability on rice by linking it to the prevailing economic reality of Iraq, where it formed the bulk of the land tax (kharaj). This ruling exemplifies the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'istihsan' (juristic preference) or adapting legal categories to new agricultural commodities not present in Medina during the Prophet's time, thereby extending the spirit of the original revelation to contemporary sustenance.
